## `write_mdim_vrt`

```python
write_mdim_vrt(ds: 'xr.Dataset', sources: 'Sequence[Any]', path: 'str | Path',
    *, composition: 'Composition', concat_dim: 'str | None' = None, crs: 'str | None' = None, sizes: 'Sequence[int] | None' = None, block_size: 'Sequence[int] | Mapping[str, Sequence[int]] | None' = None, coord_mode: 'CoordMode | Mapping[str, CoordMode]' = 'auto', inline_threshold: 'int' = 10000, require_crs: 'bool' = False, variables: 'Sequence[str] | None' = None) -> 'Path'
```

Emit a GDAL multidim VRT from an xarray Dataset.

Every data variable becomes an ``<Array>`` in one VRT (OISST-style files
with sst/anom/err/ice give one VRT with four arrays). Each source file is
expected to hold every variable; variables that lack the composition dim
(static fields such as a land mask) are read from the first source.


**Parameters**


`ds`
:   The Dataset whose shape / dims / coords / data-vars describe the
desired virtual composition.

`sources`
:   ``list[str | Path | dict]``. Dict form: ``{"path": ..., "size": N,
"array": "/name"}``; with several variables use ``"arrays": {var:
"/name", ...}`` instead of ``"array"`` for any renames (variables
not listed default to their own name).

`path`
:   Output ``.vrt`` path.

`composition`
:   ``"stack"`` | ``"concat"``. (``"mosaic"`` is reserved and raises
``NotImplementedError``.)

`concat_dim`
:   Required for stack (new dim name) and concat (existing dim name).

`crs`
:   WKT string. If omitted, we look at ``ds[dv].attrs["crs_wkt"]`` /
``ds[dv].rio.crs`` / CF ``grid_mapping``; if still absent the
writer emits no ``<SRS>`` and warns. Pass ``require_crs=True`` to make
that an error.

`sizes`
:   Convenience shortcut for concat: ``list[int]`` of per-source sizes
along ``concat_dim``. If not given, we try (in order):
per-source ``size`` in dict-form sources, ``ds.chunks[concat_dim]``
when the number of chunks matches the number of sources, then
opening each source to read ``.sizes[concat_dim]``.

`block_size`
:   Sequence matching array dim order, or dict keyed by data-var name.
``None`` falls back to the dask chunks, then to
``encoding["preferred_chunks"]`` / ``encoding["chunksizes"]``.

`coord_mode`
:   ``"auto"`` (default) | ``"inline"`` | ``"source"`` or dict per coord.

`inline_threshold`
:   In auto mode, coords with ``size <= threshold`` go inline.

`variables`
:   Subset of ``ds.data_vars`` to write, in order. Default: all data vars
except CF ``grid_mapping`` containers (their content is carried by
``<SRS>``).

`require_crs`
:   When True, raise ``VrtWriterError`` if no CRS can be
determined. Default False (warn-and-omit); matches the reality of
ocean NetCDFs and other CRS-less sources.

## `from_stac`

```python
from_stac(items: 'str | Path | Iterable[Mapping[str, Any]]', path: 'str | Path',
    *, assets: 'Sequence[str] | None' = None, dim: 'str' = 'time', crs: 'str | None' = None, block_size: 'Sequence[int] | Mapping[str, Sequence[int]] | None' = None) -> 'Path'
```

Write a multidim VRT stacking STAC items along ``dim``.


**Parameters**


`items`
:   A stac-geoparquet file (path or URL; needs ``pyarrow``), or an
iterable of STAC item dicts (``pystac.Item.to_dict()`` works). Both
the flat geoparquet layout and the nested ``"properties"`` layout are
read.

`path`
:   Output ``.vrt`` path.

`assets`
:   Asset keys to write, one array each, in this order. Default: every
asset with ``raster:bands``, in first-seen order.

`dim`
:   Name of the stack dimension (one position per distinct datetime).

`crs`
:   WKT override. Default: from the items' projection fields, turned into
WKT with ``pyproj`` (or GDAL's ``osr``) when only an EPSG code is
given, so the axis mapping can be computed.

`block_size`
:   Optional ``<BlockSize>``; the catalogue does not record it.


**Raises**


`VrtWriterError`
:   Items on different grids, duplicate datetimes, a band description
that changes between items, or no usable CRS.

## `encode_datetime_coord`

```python
encode_datetime_coord(da: 'xr.DataArray',
    *, unit: "Literal['seconds', 'minutes', 'hours', 'days']" = 'days', since: 'str' = '1970-01-01') -> 'xr.DataArray'
```

Convert a datetime64 coord DataArray to numeric + CF ``units`` attr.

Handy pre-step when you have a ``datetime64[ns]`` time coord and want to
feed it to the writer (which refuses datetime dtypes per v0 policy).

## `VrtWriterError`

Raised when the writer's rules are violated.

Subclasses ``ValueError`` so that naive except-clauses still catch it;
specific enough that callers can ``except VrtWriterError`` to distinguish
rule violations from generic bad input.

## Accessor

`import xvrt.accessor` registers `Dataset.vrt.write_mdim(path, sources=..., ...)`, which forwards its arguments to `write_mdim_vrt`.
